theme: The church as God’s field; apostolic ministry
readingInstruction: Read 1 Corinthians 3:1-4:21. Paul continues to deal with divisions by showing how God sees ministers and the church. Notice the pictures: a field, a building, a temple. Notice also what Paul says about being a steward.
settingTheScene: Paul has said that the cross confounds human wisdom. Now he applies this to the church’s attitude to its leaders. The Corinthians were comparing teachers like sports fans choosing favorite athletes. Paul wants them to see that ministers are servants and that the church is God’s own possession.
observation: “I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth” (3:6).
“For no one can lay a foundation other than that which is laid, which is Jesus Christ” (3:11).
“Do you not know that you are God’s temple and that God’s Spirit dwells in you?” (3:16).
“And you are Christ’s, and Christ is God’s” (3:23).
“This is how one should regard us, as servants of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God” (4:1).
“Moreover, it is required of stewards that they be found faithful” (4:2).
“What do you have that you did not receive?” (4:7).
“For the kingdom of God does not consist in talk but in power” (4:20).
interpretation:
Paul says he could not address them as spiritual people but as people of the flesh, infants in Christ. They were still being fed milk. Their jealousy and strife showed it. “For when one says, I follow Paul, and another, I follow Apollos, are you not being merely human?” Then he gives the right view of ministry: “What then is Apollos? What is Paul? Servants through whom you believed, as the Lord assigned to each. I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth. So neither he who plants nor he who waters is anything, but only God who gives the growth.” Ministers are workers; God is the source of life.

The church is “God’s field, God’s building.” Paul laid a foundation as a wise master builder, and others build on it. “No one can lay a foundation other than that which is laid, which is Jesus Christ.” Each builder must take care how he builds. The quality of each person’s work will be revealed on the day of judgment, tested by fire. Gold, silver, and precious stones endure; wood, hay, and straw burn. If the work survives, the builder receives a reward; if it is burned up, he suffers loss, though he himself will be saved, as through fire. This passage encourages teachers and builders to serve with care, building with the truth.

Then: “Do you not know that you are God’s temple and that God’s Spirit dwells in you? If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy him. For God’s temple is holy, and you are that temple.” Notice that “you” is plural. The church is the dwelling of God’s Spirit. Dividing the church is a serious sin because it damages God’s temple.

Paul urges them to be wise by becoming fools in the world’s eyes, “for the wisdom of this world is folly with God.” And do not boast in men. “For all things are yours, whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas or the world or life or death or the present or the future, all are yours, and you are Christ’s, and Christ is God’s.” The church does not belong to its leaders; the leaders belong to the church, and the church belongs to Christ.

In chapter 4, Paul describes true ministers as “servants of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God.” A steward manages what belongs to another, and he must be faithful. Paul does not worry about human judgment, or even his own self-assessment: “It is the Lord who judges me.” He gives a sharp contrast between the proud Corinthians, who think themselves kings, and the apostles, who are “a spectacle to the world,” “fools for Christ’s sake,” hungry and homeless, reviled and slandered. “What do you have that you did not receive? If then you received it, why do you boast as if you had not received it?” He closes as a father: “I became your father in Christ Jesus through the gospel.” And he warns that he will come, if the Lord wills, to see not the talk but the power.
connection: Isaiah 28:16 speaks of the cornerstone. Ephesians 2:19-22 says the church is a holy temple in the Lord. 1 Peter 2:4-10 describes living stones. Matthew 7:24-27 shows building on the rock. 2 Corinthians 6:16 repeats that we are the temple of the living God. 1 Timothy 3:15 calls the church the pillar and buttress of the truth. Luke 12:42-48 describes the faithful steward. Romans 11:36 speaks of all things from him. 1 Peter 5:1-4 is a charge to elders.
application:
Thank a person who planted or watered in your life. Remember that God gave the growth.

Ask what you are building with: gold, silver, or straw. How could your ministry or your work last?

Look at your gifts and abilities and ask, What do I have that I did not receive?
prayerPrompts: Thank God that he alone gives growth.
Thank him for those who planted and watered in your life.
Ask him to make Christ your only foundation.
